summary: Ralph Lilley Turner was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Christ's College (~1907–1910). He lectured at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1913), became Professor of Indian Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University (1920–1922), and served as Director of SOAS (1922–1957).

Ralph T. H. Griffith was an Indologist educated at Warminster School, Uppingham School, and The Queen's College, Oxford (BA ~1843–1846), studying under Horace Hayman Wilson (~1845–1849). He served in the Indian Education Service (~1853–1885) and as Principal of Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi (~1861–1878).
Ralph Waldo Emerson worked in philosophy and other fields. He completed his studies at Harvard College and Harvard University (~1817–1821), later attending Harvard Divinity School (~1825–1826).
Ram Chandra Dhungana worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Assistant Editor for Ancient Nepal (attested 1973) and for the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1974).

Ram Chandra Kak worked in history, archaeology, and Indology after studying at Sri Pratap College and under John Marshall. He was curator at Sri Pratap Singh Museum, Archaeological Survey of India superintendent, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Secretary (1919–1929), and Archaeological Department Superintendent (~1920–1930).

Ram Chandra Pandeya was an Indologist and philosopher working in Buddhist studies who studied under T. R. V. Murti (~1954–1957) and Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale. At the University of Delhi, he headed Buddhist Studies (~1966–1973) and served as acharya (~1973–1996).

Ram Karan Sharma was an Indologist and linguist who earned his MA at Patna University and his PhD at UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He served as vice chancellor of Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Ram Mohan Roy was active in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He founded the Atmiya Sabha (1814), Presidency University (1816), Mirat-ul-Akbar and Anglo-Hindu School (1822), Vedanta College (1826), Brahmo Samaj (1828), and the Calcutta Unitarian Committee.

Ram Niwas Pandey works in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, with Hit Narayan Jha serving as his doctoral supervisor.

Ram Shankar Bhattacharya was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Swami Dharmamegha Aranya and Raghunatha Shastri. He held posts as an अध्यापक at Tikmani Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya and as an अनुसन्धानसहायक at Banaras Hindu University and All-India Kashiraj Trust.

Ram Shankar Tripathi was an Indologist and Buddhist studies philosopher. He headed Buddhist Philosophy at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1974–1994), served as Dean of Śabdavidyā at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1994–2004), and taught at Banaras Hindu University.

Ram Sharan Sharma was a historian and Indologist who studied at Patna College, Patna University, and SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He headed history at Patna University (1958–1973), chaired the Indian Council of Historical Research (1972–1977), and held a Delhi professorship.

Rama Mishra Shastri was an Indologist and philosopher. He held academic posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, where he is attested as a Professor in 1889 and as an assistant Professor of Sáṅkhya in 1914.

Rama Nath Sharma is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Banaras Hindu University, University of Allahabad, Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University, and University of Rochester. He taught at Allahabad and Rochester before becoming a Sanskrit professor at the University of Hawaiʻi.

Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar was an Indologist and linguist educated at Elphinstone College, University of Mumbai, and University of Göttingen under Martin Haug. He held professorships at Elphinstone and Deccan College, and served as Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (~1893–1894).

Ramanatha Dikshita was an Indology scholar. He held a post in the साधूलालरिसर्चविभाग at Sarasvati Bhavana (attested 1944) and served as head of the Veda department (वेदविभागाध्यक्ष) at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi (attested 1970).

Ramaprasad Chanda was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Dhaka Collegiate School, Dhaka College, and Scottish Church College. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India, lectured at the University of Calcutta, and served as Superintendent at the Indian Museum (1921–1932).
Ramaprasada Tripathi was a scholar in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, with his tenure attested there in 1976 and 2001.

Ramaranjan Mukherji was an Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University. He served as head of Sanskrit at Jadavpur, vice chancellor at the University of Burdwan and Rabindra Bharati University, and chancellor of Rashtriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha.

Ramashastri Bhagavatacharya was an Indology scholar. In 1891, he is attested as an Assistant Professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and as a teacher/professor (अध्यापक) at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi.
